name: Plasmablastic Lymphoma
aliases: Plasmablastic lymphoma of the oral cavity

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of large neoplastic cells with plasmablastic morphology
Expression of plasma cell markers (CD138, MUM1) with absence or weak expression of B-cell markers (CD20, PAX5)
Detection of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) encoded RNA by in situ hybridization in tumor cells
Presentation with rapidly enlarging mass, often in the oral cavity or extranodal sites

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Morphologic and immunophenotypic criteria with exclusion of other lymphoma subtypes; EBV detection supportive but not mandatory
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of morphology, immunophenotype, and clinical features; molecular studies may assist in difficult cases.

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly involves the jaw or oral mucosa
Characteristic large cells with plasmacytic differentiation
searchTerms: abnormal plasma cell appearance on biopsy

common.symptomName: Extranodal tumor masses (e.g., gastrointestinal tract, lymph nodes)
searchTerms: tumors in gastrointestinal tract or lymph nodes

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
common.notes: Systemic symptoms common in aggressive lymphomas

occasional.notes: May be present in advanced disease
searchTerms: bone marrow infiltration by abnormal cells
blood cell production affected by marrow involvement

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to CNS involvement
occasional.notes: Rare but possible in advanced cases
searchTerms: neurological symptoms from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to central nervous system disease
brain or spinal cord related neurological signs

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to tumor lysis
searchTerms: kidney failure due to cell destruction

laboratory: Anemia and cytopenias in advanced disease
EBV-encoded RNA positivity in tumor cells
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing extranodal masses, often in oral cavity or gastrointestinal tract
Possible bone marrow infiltration on MRI or PET
genetic: Absence of typical B-cell lymphoma translocations (e.g., t(14;18))
other: Immunohistochemistry showing CD138+, MUM1+, CD20- or weak

distinguishingFeatures: Monoclonal protein in serum or urine
Different clinical presentation with bone marrow plasmacytosis

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging mass in oral cavity or extranodal site
Unexplained B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Immunodeficiency or HIV infection with aggressive lymphoma features
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Delecluse HJ, Anagnostopoulos I, Dallenbach F, et al. Plasmablastic lymphoma: a new aggressive variant of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Blood. 1997.
Taddesse-Heath L, Chen W, Medeiros LJ. Plasmablastic lymphoma: an update. Arch Pathol Lab Med. 2010.
